root_cause.text: In `drivers/md/raid10.c`, NOWAIT bios that fail `regular_request_wait()` were incorrectly sent to `raid_end_bio_io()/allow_barrier()`, which decremented `r10conf->nr_pending` even though NOWAIT requests never incremented it, causing `nr_pending` underflow and a barrier deadlock during array check/resync.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE text says NOWAIT requests “do not increment nr_pending in wait_barrier()” but the added `raid_end_bio_io()` from commit `43806c3d5b9b` “will unconditionally do an atomic_dec_and_test(&conf->nr_pending) even though the corresponding increment on nr_pending didn’t happen”; the patch fixes this by replacing `raid_end_bio_io(r10_bio)` with `free_r10bio(r10_bio)` in both `raid10_read_request()` and `raid10_write_request()` when `regular_request_wait()` returns false.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the raid10 read-request failure path to free the r10_bio directly instead of using the normal I/O ավարտ path.
intent_record.what: In raid10_read_request(), the failure path after regular_request_wait() no longer calls raid_end_bio_io(r10_bio); it now calls free_r10bio(r10_bio) before returning.
intent_record.how: When the request cannot proceed, the code now frees the r10_bio structure directly instead of ending bio I/O through the previous completion path. This changes the abort handling for this early-exit case so the allocated raid10 bio is released immediately.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the RAID10 write-request failure path to free the r10 bio instead of incorrectly ending its I/O completion.
intent_record.what: In raid10_write_request(), the failure path after regular_request_wait() now calls free_r10bio(r10_bio) instead of raid_end_bio_io(r10_bio) before returning.
intent_record.how: If the request cannot proceed, the code now fully releases the r10 bio object rather than ending only the bio I/O path. This changes the cleanup behavior on the early-return path and prevents the write request from being finalized through the wrong helper.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the RAID10 write-request failure path to free the r10 bio instead of incorrectly ending its I/O completion.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix RAID10 request failure handling so failed requests free the r10 bio directly rather than following the normal I/O completion path.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: failed RAID10 requests were incorrectly sent through the normal completion path, which would drop nr_pending for NOWAIT bios that never incremented it. Freeing the r10 bio directly on failure prevents the underflow and resulting barrier deadlock.

candidates.rationale: This is the incorrect completion path taken when regular_request_wait() fails for NOWAIT bios; it routes the bio through normal I/O ավարտ handling, which leads to allow_barrier()/nr_pending decrement even though the request never incremented nr_pending.
Same root cause in the write path: failed NOWAIT requests were sent to normal bio completion instead of being freed directly, causing the underflow of nr_pending and the resulting barrier deadlock.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement incorrectly sends failed NOWAIT raid10 requests through the normal I/O completion path. That path reaches allow_barrier() and decrements r10conf->nr_pending even though NOWAIT bios never incremented it, causing nr_pending underflow and a barrier deadlock.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows the vulnerable control flow around `regular_request_wait()`. In both `raid10_read_request()` and `raid10_write_request()`, the code now does `if (!regular_request_wait(mddev, conf, bio, ...)) { raid_end_bio_io(r10_bio); return; }`. This means a NOWAIT request that fails `regular_request_wait()` is sent to `raid_end_bio_io()`. Per the root cause, that path calls `allow_barrier()` / decrements `r10conf->nr_pending`, even though NOWAIT requests never incremented it, which is the buggy construct. The fix is also not present here; the diff shown is exactly the problematic behavior because it adds `raid_end_bio_io(r10_bio)` on the early return instead of avoiding that pending-count/barrier path. Therefore the vulnerable logic is present and not yet fixed in this commit version.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is specifically the NOWAIT bio path that should not increment/decrement barrier accounting. In this snippet, that handling is already present: `wait_barrier()` takes `bool nowait` and explicitly does `if (nowait) { ret = false; }` followed by `if (ret) atomic_inc(&conf->nr_pending);`, so NOWAIT requests do not increment `nr_pending`. Callers also bail out early on NOWAIT, e.g. `if (!wait_barrier(conf, bio->bi_opf & REQ_NOWAIT)) { bio_wouldblock_error(bio); return false; }`, and write/discard paths check `REQ_NOWAIT` and return before proceeding. Since the buggy behavior described (NOWAIT bios being sent onward to barrier release logic and underflowing `nr_pending`) is prevented here, the vulnerable construct is absent and the fix is already included.
